intro: If you're coming to Roi Et as a larger group or a whole family and want more private space than a single hotel room, YaYa Hostel is worth a look. Despite the word 'hostel' in the name, this is really an entire house for rent — 3 bedrooms, 3 private bathrooms, around 150 sqm — booked as a whole, not a dorm with bunk beds. It's in central Roi Et, near Bueng Phlan Chai and walkable to the city centre, with parking for self-drivers, from around ฿1,200/night for the whole house. Real guest reviews praise getting a whole house that works out cheap split between people, with a living area and a kitchen to cook your own meals, like staying at a friend's place. Just note that as a small host-run rental, there aren't many platform reviews yet, so it's worth messaging the host to confirm details and the latest condition before booking.

body.html: YaYa Hostel is an entire house for rent in the municipal area of Roi Et, in the Nai Mueang subdistrict. On booking platforms like Agoda it's clearly listed as a house with 3 bedrooms, 3 private bathrooms and around 150 square metres of space. The reason people choose it is simple: you get a whole house to yourselves, with no shared space, several bedrooms so people can split up, enough bathrooms for everyone, and a common area to hang out together. It works well for multi-generational families, groups of friends, or parties in town for a merit-making event, a wedding, or a Roi Et trip together.

The real strength of renting a whole house is privacy and value when you split it between several people. With 5–6 of you, the whole-house rate works out to just a few hundred baht each — cheaper than booking several hotel rooms. You get a kitchen or kitchenette to cook your own food, a fridge to store things, and a living area to socialise at night without disturbing anyone. The bedrooms have air-con, and there's Wi-Fi and parking for self-drivers. Many guests like the 'staying at a friend's place' feel — more flexible than a hotel, where you can come and go whenever, cook, and sit up talking as long as you like.

"Came with the whole family and got a whole house — comfortably split the bedrooms, with a living area to relax in the evening. Worked out really cheap split between us, and the central location meant Bueng Phlan Chai was just a short drive."

The location is in central Roi Et, in the Nai Mueang area. It's close to Bueng Phlan Chai, the central lake park that's Roi Et's landmark, a short drive or walk away. It's within a short drive of Roi Et Tower, Wat Burapha Phiram (home to Thailand's tallest standing Buddha), Wat Klang Ming Muang, and the big malls — Big C and Robinson. The surrounding area is a residential city neighbourhood with restaurants, coffee shops, markets and convenience stores, so finding food is easy, and Roi Et Airport (ROI) is about a 15–20 minute drive. This suits groups who want to stay central, stroll around Bueng Phlan Chai morning and evening, and have their own car for temple-hopping around town.

To be straight with you, based on real reviews: YaYa Hostel is a small, host-run rental that doesn't have many platform reviews yet. The upside is dealing directly with the host and being able to sort out details; the limitation is that service isn't as systematic as a hotel chain — check-in usually means arranging a time with the host, and there's no 24-hour front desk. Because it's a house, not a hotel, there's no daily housekeeping, breakfast or on-site staff — you look after the place among yourselves. The condition of the house and furniture depends on the owner's upkeep, so check the latest photos and ask the host what's provided (kitchen equipment, washing machine, hot water) before booking. And if you're only 1–2 people, renting the whole house may not be as good value as a single hotel room.

Bottom line: YaYa Hostel suits groups of friends or families who want a whole house to themselves in central Roi Et, with private space, a kitchen to cook in, and the flexibility to do their own thing. With several of you splitting the cost, it's better value and more comfortable than booking multiple hotel rooms. But if you're travelling solo or as a couple, or you want hotel-style service with a front desk and breakfast, a budget chain like Hop Inn or a city hotel will likely suit you better. The trick is to message the host before every booking to confirm numbers, check-in time and what's in the house.

A tip from following the reviews here: confirm whether the rate you see is for the whole house or per room, and how many people the house sleeps, since house rentals usually have a guest cap. If you're a big party, ask the host about extra bedding and parking for several cars in advance. As there's no breakfast on-site, head out to eat over by Bueng Phlan Chai or a morning market in town for a meal the way Roi Et locals do it. And compare the whole-house rate on Agoda against booking several hotel rooms — for larger groups, the whole house usually comes out ahead.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — YaYa Hostel Roi Et

faq.q: Is YaYa Hostel Roi Et a dorm hostel or an entire house?
faq.a: Despite the word 'hostel' in the name, YaYa Hostel is really an entire house for rent — 3 bedrooms, 3 private bathrooms, around 150 sqm. You book the whole house, not a bunk in a shared dorm, which makes it well suited to groups and families who want private space.

faq.q: Where is YaYa Hostel Roi Et, and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's in central Roi Et, in the Nai Mueang area, close to Bueng Phlan Chai, the central lake park that's the city's landmark. It's a short drive to Roi Et Tower, Wat Burapha Phiram, Wat Klang Ming Muang and the big malls like Big C and Robinson. Roi Et Airport is about a 15–20 minute drive away.

faq.q: How much does YaYa Hostel cost, and how do you book?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿1,200/night for the whole house, rising over holidays and festivals. You book the entire house, so split between several people it works out to a few hundred baht each. Compare the rate on Agoda against booking multiple hotel rooms, and message the host to confirm numbers before booking.

faq.q: Who is YaYa Hostel best for?
faq.a: It's best for groups of friends and families travelling together who want a whole house to themselves, with private space, a kitchen and the flexibility to do their own thing. If you're solo or a couple, or want hotel-style service, a city hotel or a budget chain like Hop Inn will likely suit you better.

faq.q: Does YaYa Hostel have a kitchen and parking — is breakfast included?
faq.a: Yes — there's a kitchen or kitchenette to cook your own meals, plus Wi-Fi and parking for self-drivers. But because it's a house, not a hotel, there's no breakfast or daily housekeeping. Head out to eat near Bueng Phlan Chai or a morning market in town instead.

faq.q: Anything to know before booking YaYa Hostel?
faq.a: As a small, host-run rental, there aren't many platform reviews yet. Check-in means arranging a time with the host, with no 24-hour front desk. Check the latest photos, ask what's provided (kitchen, washing machine, hot water) and confirm how many people the house sleeps before every booking.
